title: Integration of the resources of a proven health and healing forest in combination with mindfulness and relaxation procedures in the overall treatment plan of soldiers of the Bundeswehr with anxiety symptoms during full inpatient treatment
summary:
This study aims to demonstrate the effectiveness of forest therapy in the treatment of anxiety symptoms. Forest therapy is a combination of complementary physical and mental exercises in a suitable forest environment that results in reduced heart rate, blood pressure and stress levels, while strengthening the immune system, breathing, physical and mental fitness and well-being.
It is assumed that the special forest climate is suitable for health promotion, prevention and therapy of anxiety disorders. Healing forests are forest areas designed for therapeutic use for special indications. Treatment by trained therapists in healing forests can have a beneficial effect on diseases and disabilities as well as mental disorders and alleviate chronic diseases.
Other positive effects are an improvement in the ability to concentrate and self-confidence, as well as a reduction in anxiety and an increase in mood and well-being. However, there is a need for further research on the health-promoting or therapeutic effects of a stay in the forest.
As part of the study, the data determined in the course of routine treatment is to be recorded and evaluated for our study over a period of 6 weeks. This includes the following data: age, gender, physical and psychiatric comorbidities, results of the psychological test sheets.
For the study, in addition to the regular inpatient, multimodal therapy program, so-called forest therapy units take place once a week at a fixed time in the Lahnsteiner Heilwald, accompanied by the study director and a specialist nurse for psychiatry and psychotherapy.
A therapy session is scheduled for 180 minutes. There will be no further therapy offers for you on this day (e.g. individual, group therapy, ergotherapy, physiotherapy). During the individual therapy units, a fixed tour is completed, which leads past a total of 6 therapy stations.
An exercise module is assigned to each therapy station. These modules address the areas of mindfulness, relaxation, enjoyment, coping with stress, activating resources and strengthening personal responsibility.
For better comparability and predictability, this study is carried out with a group of patients who take part in forest therapy and a so-called control group, which takes a walk in the field, but without specific interventions.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria are the presence of one of the above-mentioned anxiety disorders, age, consent of the subject to the presented therapeutic measures as well as non-fulfilment or non-existence of the exclusion criteria.
Exclusion criteria:
The exclusion criteria are as follows: high dissociation tendency, psychotic experience, harm to own to others, mental retardation, a reduced ability to stabilize oneself, acute intoxication as well a manifest personality disorder.
